reader.requirement: FUNCTION MEDIAN returns the content of the argument-1 that holds the middle value once all argument-1 values (ALL-expanded, ODO at current count, any numeric usage, scaling and sign, expressions) are arranged in algebraic order by the simple-condition rules.

edition-consulted.switches: the function's IntroducedIn (85 for MAX, MEAN, MEDIAN) against DialectLevel: COBOL1502 before it
construct numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: at 85 a numeric function written where an identifier stands is refused (COBOL0900); inside an arithmetic expression it is not consulted
OPTIONS ARITHMETIC mode; at 85 no ARITHMETIC clause exists so Options.Arithmetic is Native, the latest edition's default arm

reader.notes: MedianScaled sorts a copy of the scale-aligned values (MedianDec on the SDIDI lane) and takes the middle at scale+1 through checked ExactMul, so the selection is algebraic and an 18-digit middle does not wrap. Same output at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: meanctx2-001 at --std 85: C8 IF MEDIAN (W1 W2 W1) = W1 true (odd count returns the content), CD MEDIAN (TQE (ALL 2) TQE (1 ALL)) over 2,8,1,2,3 = 2, CJ MEDIAN (3 - 1, W1 * 10, 0.5 + 0.5) of expressions = 1, CK MEDIAN (FUNCTION MAX (1 3) 2 9 1) = 2.5, CA MEDIAN (FUNCTION MEAN (1 2) 1 2) = 1.5, CH MEDIAN (-0 -1 1 0) = 0; degen-001 G4 MEDIAN (W-N) = -1.25 (one argument). numplace-001: DISPLAY FUNCTION MEDIAN (1 2) refused COBOL0900 at 85, so the DISPLAY device arm (FunctionDeviceText) is not reachable at this edition. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.25.4 RV1 'the content of the argument-1 having the middle value'.
